_why: THE READ CLASS, DECIDED. Twenty-three references that no rule may touch, each
resolved by reading the sentence it sits in. `rewrite-refs.py --rule read` lists
them; this file records what a reader decided, so the decision survives a replay.
AS EXACT REPLACEMENTS AND NOT AS A PATCH. The replay applies the rules to every
commit's TREE, so the read-class decisions have to apply the same way. A patch
would need the file to look the same in all 28 trees and it does not; a replacement
that finds nothing in a given tree simply does not fire, which is correct — the
TWO OLD CHAPTERS ARE AMBIGUOUS AND THE ANSWERS ARE NOT THE MAP'S HALVES.
The map splits old 12 into new 4 and new 25. But the channel-endpoint work from old
12's own commit (`6c1c90b`) sits in the REBUILD's chapter 8 span, because new 8's
subject is the endpoints. So eight of the ten `chapter 3.12` references mean new 8 —
this chapter — and two mean the outsider milestone at new 26, which is old 14's
second half and not old 12's at all. Neither answer is derivable from the map.
